newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard criticized over Japan park name.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard criticized over Japan park name.

text.p: A move by Australian Prime Minister John Howard to drop the word "peace" from the name of a planned joint Australian-Japanese park in Canberra has drawn fire ahead of an expected visit by Japan's prime minister.

A committee for Canberra and the Japanese city of Nara agreed to drop "peace" from the name of the Canberra-Nara Peace Park after Howard threatened to veto the park, two weeks before the visit by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
"We are absolutely amazed and shocked that the prime minister would insist that we drop the word peace," committee chairman Brian Jones told The Canberra Times newspaper.
"... clearly, Mr Howard does not believe we have a genuine peace with Japan, as, in his mind, it has failed to properly apologise for World War Two."
Howard's office would not say if he planned to raise the issue of a Japanese apology, also sought by some other regional countries, during his talks with Hashimoto late this month.
Japan is Australia's major trading partner, with Australia running a A$5.6 billion (US$4.4 billion) surplus on total two-way trade of A$27.2 billion in the year to June 30, 1996.

Howard, whose government can over-ride Canberra municipal authorities in some planning matters in the capital, backed the country's peak veterans' organisation, the Returned Services League, in objecting to the use of the word peace.

"The (name) would suggest that Australia as a nation has absolved Japan of her war-time guilt and of course we have not done that," league president retired Major-General Digger James said this month.
A spokesman for Howard told Reuters the prime minister felt the league's sensitivities should be taken into account.
"The removal of the word 'peace' represents a sensible compromise," he said.
